statement: DERIVED — a statistical realisation of the Reid+2019 arm model, not a catalogue of real stars.
description: A deterministically seeded point cloud sampling the Milky Way stellar disk, bar and bulge. The spiral overdensity is sampled directly from the log-periodic fits in arms.json. No point in this file corresponds to any real star. It exists because there is no photograph of the Milky Way from outside and there never will be.
layout: Struct-of-Arrays (all x, then all y, then all z, then all colourIndex), little-endian

quantization.position: none — x, y, z are IEEE-754 float32 parsecs, no scale or offset applied

colour.inverse: colourIndex = round(255 * log10(T_K / 2000)), T clamped to [2000, 20000] K
colour.note: Temperature here is a colour parameter for an age/metallicity gradient, NOT a measured effective temperature of anything.

colour.paletteFormat: sRGB 0..255 triples, index i corresponds to T = 2000 * 10 ** (i / 255) K
colour.derivation: Planck spectral radiance integrated 360-830 nm against the CIE 1931 2-deg observer (Wyman, Sloan & Shirley 2013 multi-lobe Gaussian fits), XYZ -> linear sRGB, negative components clipped, normalised so the largest linear component is 1 (chromaticity only; brightness is the renderer's business), then sRGB gamma-encoded.

frame.name: Galactocentric galactic Cartesian
frame.axes: +X along galactic rotation at the Sun (toward l=90deg); +Y from the Galactic centre toward the Sun; +Z toward the North Galactic Pole. Right-handed.

epoch: present day (static; no proper motion or rotation is baked in)

determinism.guarantee: A single mulberry32 stream drives every draw in generation order (bulge, bar, disk, arms). Re-running this script on any machine reproduces field.bin byte-for-byte, which is what makes a shared permalink show every user the identical galaxy.

bulge.shape: boxy/peanut: exponential radial profile, axis ratios 1 : 0.5 : 0.45
bulge.temperatureK: 3300 + 1500 * u^1.4 — old and metal-rich, so red

bar.angleConvention: Angle between the bar long axis and the Sun-Galactic-centre line, near end at positive galactic longitude.
bar.angleSource: Wegg, Gerhard & Portail 2015, MNRAS 450, 4050 (bar angle 27 +/- 2 deg)

disk.temperatureK: (4150 + 950 * min(2.2, R/R0)) * exp(0.2 * N(0,1)), thick disk * 0.9; 2% hot tail at 9000-18000 K. Encodes an inside-out age/metallicity gradient: redder inward.

arms.sampledFrom: arms.json — the Reid+2019 log-periodic fits, evaluated over betaDrawRangeDeg
arms.radialFalloff: accept with probability min(1, exp(-(R - 2 kpc) / 6 kpc))
arms.crossSection: Gaussian perpendicular offset of 1-sigma = 2 * w(R) / cos(pitch), with w(R) the Reid+2019 fitted arm width plus its 42 pc/kpc gradient.
arms.armWidthScaleRationale: The Reid+2019 fitted width describes high-mass star-forming regions, a narrow ridge tracer. The broader stellar arm population is wider, so the fitted width is scaled by 2. This is a presentation choice, not a measurement.
arms.verticalProfile: double-sided exponential, flared, truncated at |z| <= 4 * h_z(R)
arms.temperatureK: 35% drawn from 7000 + 13000 * u^1.6 (the young, hot population), 65% from (4700 + 2300 * u) * exp(0.18 * N(0,1)). Net effect: arms read blue against a red disk.

source.paper: Reid M.J., Menten K.M., Brunthaler A., et al. 2019, ApJ, 885, 131
source.barGeometry: Wegg C., Gerhard O., Portail M. 2015, MNRAS 450, 4050 (2015MNRAS.450.4050W)

licence: The generated point cloud is an original work of this project and carries no third-party licence. The arm parameters it was generated from are from Reid et al. 2019 (ApJ) — see LICENSE.md in this directory.
attribution: Milky Way disk field: DERIVED — a statistical realisation of the Reid et al. (2019) arm model, not a catalogue of real stars.
reader: const x = new Float32Array(buf, 0, N)        // pc
const y = new Float32Array(buf, 4*N, N)      // pc
const z = new Float32Array(buf, 8*N, N)      // pc
const c = new Uint8Array(buf, 12*N, N)       // palette index
// Float32Array views require a 4-byte-aligned offset; 0, 4N and 8N always satisfy that.
